title: Request Flow Inspector — probe notes and interaction sketches
content:
Purpose:
Capture exploratory interaction notes and low-fidelity wireframe ideas for a Request Flow Inspector (desktop web) that helps engineers trace request ancestry, inspect span-level metadata, and rapidly filter/compare traces. This is a working doc for grooming and for pairing with engineering on feasibility and perf impact.

Context / problem we want to solve:
- Teams currently use the trace viewer to debug latency but find it hard to: follow asynchronous parent/child hops across services, compare two traces quickly, and apply composable filters that persist across sessions.
- Console traces must support both a quick triage flow (single-click to identify the slowest span) and deep investigation (pin, diff, correlate logs and metrics).

Primary UX goals:
- Make the critical path visible: highlight the end-to-end span chain that caused the request tail latency.
- Fast pivoting: allow users to pivot from a span to related logs/metrics/alerts without leaving the trace context.
- Flexible filtering: allow building compound filters (service, route, status, tag, duration > X) and saving them as reusable quick-filters.
- Lightweight compare mode: side-by-side or overlay two traces to see where latency diverges.

Key interaction sketches and notes (low-fidelity):
1) Overview strip (top of trace viewer)
   - Small, horizontal breadcrumb: Root request → service A → service B → service C
   - Quick stats badges: total latency, slowest span (name + duration), error count, sampling rate
   - Actions: Open in compare, Pin trace, Export snapshot, Link to alert

2) Waterfall + timeline canvas (center pane)
   - Left column: collapsible span tree (service.icon, span name, short tags) with keyboard nav (j/k to move, enter to expand).
   - Main canvas: waterfall bars with per-span color coding (green < 50ms, amber 50-250ms, red > 250ms) + micro-annotations for cache hits, retries, throttles.
   - Hover tooltip: full span metadata (start/end, trace-id, span-id, tags, host), copy-to-clipboard buttons for IDs.
   - Feature: "Highlight critical path" toggle — dims non-critical spans to focus on the latency chain.

3) Span inspector rail (right slide-over)
   - Opens when a span is clicked. Contains: full JSON-ish fields, sampled logs, related metrics (p95 p50), and links to the corresponding request logs.
   - Read-only/Editable annotation area: user can add a note that persists for that span in the session (not in long-term storage yet).
   - Quick actions: Jump-to-parent, Jump-to-child, Open in logs, Create incident (prefilled with span summary).

4) Compact mode and density controls
   - Toggle between Full / Compact / Minimal row density. Useful when scanning very wide traces. Compact mode collapses uninteresting child spans by default (configurable).

5) Smart filter builder (left rail)
   - Multiselect chips for service, status code, tag keys, duration range.
   - "Suggest filters" button: suggests filters based on anomalies in trace (e.g., show spans with >2 retries in last 5s).
   - Ability to save a filter as a Quick Filter; persisted to user preferences.

6) Compare mode
   - Split view: trace A (left) vs trace B (right) aligned by root timestamp with optional overlay mode where bars are stacked and color-coded by trace.
   - Auto-align heuristics: align on root start or align on a selected span (useful to compare a specific service latency).
   - Diff highlights: spans present in one trace but not the other, or spans whose duration diverges > 30%.

Backlog grooming notes (candidate tickets):
- PROD-5732: Inspector rail MVP (span metadata + logs link + quick actions). Priority: P0 for devtools customers.
- PROD-5733: Critical path highlighting algorithm (heuristics + UI toggle). Needs perf benchmark on large traces.
- PROD-5734: Compact row density + keyboard navigation for span tree. Accessibility pass required.
- PROD-5735: Smart filter builder + save quick-filters. Add backend index for tag suggestions.
- PROD-5736: Compare mode basic (side-by-side) + overlay prototype. Risk: alignment logic complexity.

Acceptance criteria (for a first usable iteration):
- Users can open a trace and identify the slowest span within 5s of load on typical trace sizes (<=100 spans).
- Clicking a span opens the inspector rail with logs and a Jump-to-parent action that navigates the waterfall.
- Filters can be composed and applied to the visible trace set and saved as a quick-filter.

Open questions / technical constraints:
- How do we compute the "critical path" deterministically for traces with async messaging (events and pub/sub)? Proposal: combine span parent-child timestamps with causal tags; if no direct parent, infer by nearest ancestor with matching request id and service tag. Need to surface the heuristic.
- Memory and rendering limitations for traces > 2k spans. Consider sampling or incremental render + progressive expansion.
- Data model: do we store user-saved quick-filters in Console backend or in browser localStorage? Tradeoff: multi-device persistence vs. complexity.

Accessibility & keyboard flows (rough):
- Focus: span tree is keyboard focusable; Enter expands, Space opens inspector rail.
- Shortcuts: "f" focuses filter input, "/" opens quick search, "c" toggles compare mode.

Design constraints / performance notes for engineering:
- Minimize DOM nodes: use canvas/virtualized list for waterfall bars.
- Tooltips should be rendered on demand; avoid full JSON parse on initial load.
- Inspector rail should fetch expanded logs lazily when opened.

UX validation plan / next steps:
- 1: Quick guerrilla usability test with 4 backend engineers: task: find root cause of a 750ms trace, compare two traces with similar roots. Collect task completion time and pain points.
- 2: Prototype a compare overlay in storybook (non-production data) and demo in team sync.
- 3: Groom backlog tickets with SRE/serving-runtime to confirm data availability and potential schema changes.

Misc notes / loose ideas:
- Heatmap overlay: timeline lane that shows p95 over time for the selected span type. Could be a separate feature once inspector is stable.
- Auto-detect noisy spans: detect low-cardinality spans with high variance and suggest a filter.
- Leak the heuristic for alignment/diff to the user in a small info pill — transparency for debugging.

Meeting captures (from 2026-03-04 sync):
- Marcus: want Jump-to-log to include HTTP headers by default; privacy check for PII needed.
- Sofia: compare overlay should be the default for perf-oriented users; add a preference toggle.
- Jordan: suggested adding "pin span" so you can freeze a span across trace switches for quick comparison.

Next immediate actions:
- Create skeleton Figma frames: Overview strip, Waterfall canvas, Inspector rail, Filter builder (Asha).
- Engineering spike: measure render perf for 1k vs 5k spans (Marcus).
- Write acceptance tests and keyboard shortcut mapping (Jordan).

Edge-case examples to validate in QA:
- Traces with merged spans (same timestamp) where parent/child ordering is ambiguous.
- Traces with missing start times for spans (fallback to log event ordering).
- Very wide traces from burst traffic with repeated retries.

This doc is intentionally exploratory. Use it to seed grooming and to align on the minimal first shipable set. Add comments below or annotate the Figma frames when available.
